title: North American Breeding Bird Survey, BCR 7, Taiga Shield and Hudson Plains: run totals of 180 bird taxa on 19 roadside routes, 1973-2025
creator: Ziolkowski, David J., Jr.; Lutmerding, Michael; Skalos, Shannon M. (U.S. Geological Survey, Eastern Ecological Science Center); English, Willow B.; Hudson, Marie-Anne R. (Environment and Climate Change Canada, Canadian Wildlife Service)

abstract: The North American Breeding Bird Survey: each breeding season, mostly in June, a skilled observer drives a roadside route of about 39.2 km and counts every bird seen within 400 m or heard at 50 stops per route, one run per route and year (a route-year can have a replicate or secondary-observer run). This table holds the 160 runs on the 19 routes of Bird Conservation Region 7 (Taiga Shield and Hudson Plains) in Manitoba, Newfoundland and Labrador, Northwest Territories, Quebec, 1973-2025. One row per run and bird taxon: y is the run total over the stops (breeding-category plus non-breeder records), zero for each of the 180 taxa recorded in this region's runs and not seen on that run. The run's date, observer, weather, start and end time, the last stop with evidence of sampling and the non-breeder part of y come with it; route coordinates are in the __units table.
samplingProtocol: North American Breeding Bird Survey: 3-minute point counts of all birds seen within 400 m or heard at 50 stops per route, spaced about 800 m along a roadside route of about 39.2 km, once per year in the breeding season (mostly June), beginning 30 minutes before local sunrise, by one observer (an assistant may record); y is the run total over the stops.
closure: period = year (index year - 1965); occasion = rank of the run within its route-year by date, start time and RPID, so a route-year with several runs is several occasions and a route-year with one run has occasion 1. A table's rows across years are not a closed population, and the run is a total over its stops. Stops are sequential spatial points about 800 m apart along a route of about 39.2 km, counted once, in one morning of about five hours, by one moving observer: they are not temporal repeats at one place, so no closure of the kind that N-mixture or occupancy models assume holds across stops.
surveyEvidenceNote: Weather.csv lists every run (one row per run, 160 here), so the survey set is a sample table. Pool: every taxon recorded in this table's runs in the breeding (States) or the non-breeder (MigrantSummary) files, in any year; observers record every bird at every run, so a zero against a taxon recorded in the region is a fair not-detected, and a taxon never recorded in this region's runs has no rows. Before 1999 the non-breeder files hold almost nothing, so a zero then with obs_nonbreeder_count NA cannot exclude a non-breeder.
geographicCoverage: Bird Conservation Region 7 (Taiga Shield and Hudson Plains; BCR code and name as in this release's Routes.csv and metadata), roadside routes in Manitoba, Newfoundland and Labrador, Northwest Territories, Quebec; route start points as published

coordinatesCoarsened.method: route start points as USGS publishes them; agency coordinates are kept as published under E7

covariateNote: obs_nonbreeder_count: NA before 1999 where no non-breeder record exists, 0 from 1999 where none does. obs_last_stop: the last stop with evidence of sampling, 1997 on (NA before). Codes, from the release metadata: wind is Beaufort 0 to 8; sky is 0 clear or few clouds, 1 partly cloudy or variable, 2 cloudy or overcast, 4 fog or smoke, 5 drizzle, 7 snow, 8 showers; obs_assistant is 1 if an assistant recorded the data; obs_quality_current is 1 if the run met all quality criteria (manual inspection before 1997, by rule from 1997); minutes are after midnight; wind or sky code 9 (no data) is NA.
designNote: One row per run and taxon; y = run total. occasion orders runs within a route-year. 126 of the 160 runs have RunType 1 (obs_run_type).

notShipped.TotalSpp: per-run count of breeding records; equals the number of breeding records of every one of the 160 runs (asserted); not shipped
notShipped.StopTotal: per-taxon number of stops with the taxon, 6,418 breeding records of this table's runs; before 1997 it is impossible in 322 records nationally; not shipped (it would also need a stop-level merge for the 18 breeding/non-breeder pairs)
notShipped.stop_and_block_level: the 10-stop blocks and per-stop counts of this table's runs (120 runs from 1997 have 50-StopData rows) are in the deposit; only BCR 15 is built at that level, for size

notes: BCR codes and names are this release's (1 to 37); bbsBayes2 has since renumbered some. USGS and bbsBayes2 analyse RunType 1 only: filter obs_run_type == 1. RPID 501/502 (experimental) lower counts on average (Sauer et al. 2019, doi:10.1093/condor/duz009). Non-breeder records are nearly absent before 1999, when the survey began to keep them: a zero then with obs_nonbreeder_count NA cannot exclude a non-breeder, and y steps up at 1999 for such taxa. y - obs_nonbreeder_count (NA as 0) is the published breeding count in every year. taxon_nonbreeder_share_1999on in __taxa is the national share of a taxon's records from 1999 that are non-breeder records (records, not birds; NA with no record from 1999). taxon_first_year and taxon_last_year in __taxa are national; a zero before taxon_first_year can mean the category did not exist yet. Unidentified groups, forms and hybrids are their own taxa, with nothing rolled up. Route covariates and route start points (not bird locations) are in __units, so eco_to_unmarked() starts with empty siteCovs; join on unit. Temperatures are as recorded, value plus scale; impossible values are kept. period = year - 1965 in every table, with the calendar year in __periods, which lists every year from the table's first to its last; a year without a run has n_runs = 0. 2020 had no field work (no row in any data file), so period 55 never occurs. eco_to_unmarked(family = "colext") builds numPrimary = max(period) and one column per (period, occasion) present, so a year without a run breaks it or misaligns it: filter to occasion == 1 and pad the periods yourself before fitting a dynamic occupancy model. occasion is the rank of the run in its route-year; every route-year here has one run. Rationale: notes/decisions/bbs_design.md.
